title: The Shining
author: Stephen King
summary: A psychological horror novel about a family isolated in a haunted hotel during winter. Perfect for students interested in psychological thrillers and suspense.

title: It
author: Stephen King
summary: An epic horror novel featuring a group of friends battling a shape-shifting entity in their hometown. A must-read for horror enthusiasts.

title: The Haunting of Hill House
author: Shirley Jackson
summary: A classic gothic horror about four researchers investigating a supposedly haunted mansion. Atmospheric and deeply unsettling.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
summary: A timeless tale of love, ambition, and the American Dream. Essential reading for students studying literature.

title: To Kill a Mockingbird
author: Harper Lee
summary: A gripping story about race, justice, and growing up in the American South. A cornerstone of modern literature.

title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
summary: A romantic novel exploring themes of love, social status, and personal growth. Perfect for literature and romance lovers.

author: George Orwell
summary: A dystopian novel depicting a totalitarian society. Essential for understanding political themes and philosophical concepts.

title: The Odyssey
author: Homer
summary: An ancient epic poem describing Odysseus's journey home after the Trojan War. Foundation of Western literature.

title: A Brief History of Time
author: Stephen Hawking
summary: A groundbreaking exploration of black holes, the Big Bang, and the nature of time. Perfect for science-minded students.

title: Sapiens
author: Yuval Noah Harari
summary: A fascinating overview of human history from the Stone Age to modernity. Excellent for understanding civilization.

title: The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich
author: William L. Shirer
summary: A comprehensive history of Nazi Germany. Essential reading for understanding World War II.

title: Thinking, Fast and Slow
author: Daniel Kahneman
summary: An exploration of human psychology and decision-making. Invaluable for understanding cognitive biases.

title: Atomic Habits
author: James Clear
summary: A practical guide to building better habits and breaking bad ones. Perfect for students seeking self-improvement.

title: Deep Work
author: Cal Newport
summary: Rules for focused success in a distracted world. Essential reading for students serious about productivity.

title: The Lean Startup
author: Eric Ries
summary: A guide to building successful startups with minimal resources. Great for entrepreneurial students.

title: How to Win Friends and Influence People
author: Dale Carnegie
summary: A timeless guide to interpersonal skills and communication. Beneficial for all students.

title: The Road Not Taken
author: Robert Frost
summary: A collection of poetry exploring themes of choice, nature, and life. Ideal for literature students.

title: Paradise Lost
author: John Milton
summary: An epic poem depicting the fall of Satan and Adam's temptation. A masterpiece of English literature.

title: Leaves of Grass
author: Walt Whitman
summary: A collection of poems celebrating human experience and nature. Influential for American literature.

title: The Raven
author: Edgar Allan Poe
summary: A gothic narrative poem of psychological terror. Perfect for poetry and horror enthusiasts.

title: Howl
author: Allen Ginsberg
summary: A controversial poem capturing the Beat Generation spirit. Important for understanding modern poetry.

title: The Godfather
author: Mario Puzo
summary: A legendary novel about the Corleone crime family. Basis for the iconic film trilogy.

title: Jaws
author: Peter Benchley
summary: A thrilling tale of a great white shark terrorizing a beach town. Basis for Spielberg's classic film.

title: The Hunger Games
author: Suzanne Collins
summary: A dystopian adventure about survival and rebellion. Perfect for fans of action and adventure.

title: Dune
author: Frank Herbert
summary: An epic science fiction novel set on a desert planet. A complex and rewarding read.

title: The Matrix
author: Lana Wachowski, Lilly Wachowski
summary: A revolutionary science fiction concept exploring reality and consciousness. Influential film property.

title: The Silence of the Lambs
author: Thomas Harris
summary: A gripping psychological thriller featuring an FBI trainee and a brilliant serial killer. Masterful tension building.

title: The Stand
author: Stephen King
summary: An epic post-apocalyptic horror novel about survivors of a devastating plague. King's longest work.

title: The Catcher in the Rye
author: J.D. Salinger
summary: A coming-of-age story about teenage alienation and angst. A classic of American literature.

title: Wuthering Heights
author: Emily Brontë
summary: A dark romantic novel set on the Yorkshire moors. Features complex characters and passionate relationships.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
summary: A pioneering novel featuring an independent female protagonist. Important for feminist literature.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
summary: A groundbreaking gothic novel about scientific ambition and creation. The first science fiction novel.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
summary: An epistolary horror novel about a vampire's invasion of England. A classic of Gothic literature.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
author: Alexandre Dumas
summary: An adventure novel about revenge and redemption. A thrilling tale of escape and fortune.

title: Les Misérables
author: Victor Hugo
summary: An epic novel of justice, redemption, and love during the French Revolution. Lengthy but rewarding.

title: The Metamorphosis
author: Franz Kafka
summary: A surreal novella about a man transformed into an insect. Explores existential themes.

title: Crime and Punishment
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: A psychological novel about a student who commits murder. Explores guilt and redemption.

title: War and Peace
author: Leo Tolstoy
summary: An epic novel spanning the Napoleonic Wars. A monumental work of literature.

title: Anna Karenina
author: Leo Tolstoy
summary: A novel about love, marriage, and society in 19th century Russia. A tragedy of passion.

title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky
summary: A philosophical novel about faith, doubt, and morality. A profound exploration of human nature.

title: Mulan
author: Various (Literary Adaptations)
summary: Based on a legendary Chinese warrior woman. A story of courage and identity.

title: The Lion King
author: Various (Literary Adaptations)
summary: An epic tale of a lion prince's journey to reclaim his throne. Rich with themes of responsibility.

title: Sonnet 18
author: William Shakespeare
summary: Shakespeare's most famous sonnet celebrating beauty and immortality. A masterpiece of English poetry.

title: The Iliad
author: Homer
summary: The legendary account of the Trojan War. Foundation of Western epic poetry.

title: A Tale of Two Cities
author: Charles Dickens
summary: A novel set during the French Revolution featuring love and sacrifice. Famous for redemption themes.

title: Great Expectations
author: Charles Dickens
summary: A coming-of-age novel about ambition and social class in Victorian England. Explores personal growth.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
author: Oscar Wilde
summary: A psychological novel about vanity and corruption. A gothic tale of moral decay.

title: Sense and Sensibility
author: Jane Austen
summary: A novel contrasting emotional and rational approaches to life and love. Austen's debut novel.

title: Emma
author: Jane Austen
summary: A witty novel about a young woman's romantic misadventures and personal growth. Austen's most uplifting work.

title: Persuasion
author: Jane Austen
summary: A romantic novel about second chances and enduring love. Austen's final completed novel.

title: Rebecca
author: Daphne du Maurier
summary: A gothic mystery about a new wife haunted by her husband's first wife. Psychological suspense at its finest.

title: The Grapes of Wrath
author: John Steinbeck
summary: An epic novel about a family's struggle during the Great Depression. A powerful social commentary.

title: Of Mice and Men
author: John Steinbeck
summary: A novella about friendship and the American Dream. A poignant tale of hope and tragedy.

title: The Yellow Wallpaper
author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman
summary: A short story about a woman's psychological breakdown. An early feminist critique of medical treatment.

title: Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?
author: Philip K. Dick
summary: A science fiction novel exploring consciousness and reality. Basis for the Blade Runner films.
